answers.explanation: Each holds the lock the other needs, and neither will let go.
Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and a cycle of waiting. Break any one and deadlock is impossible.
If every thread takes locks in the same global order, no cycle can form.
Source-first deadlocks when two transfers go in opposite directions. Id order is the same for every thread.
That's why application code that uses transactions needs retry logic.
Each thread holds one and waits for the other's.
